title: DevX Onboarding Playlist and Support Handbook: SDK Quickstarts, API Examples, Docs Ops
author: Monica Alvarez
content:
Overview:
This document is a compact, hands-on playlist for new and ramping engineers who author or maintain developer-facing artifacts: language SDK quickstarts, canonical API examples, docs-site snippet operations and publishing, and the support handoff checklist. It aims to make an engineer or integrator productive within 12 days and to codify canonical fixes for frequent support issues.

Audience:
- SDK engineers, technical writers, and platform integrators
- Solutions engineers and customer success engineers who ship examples
- Support engineers performing first- and second-line triage

Objectives and measurable outcomes:
- Time-to-first-success: target 2 hours to run a sample call against sandbox and get expected output.
- Docs CI stability: docs-build-runner daily success >= 99%.
- Snippet CI pass: snippet-validator pass rate >= 98%.
- Support handoff completeness: 100% of escalations include minimal repro, logs, and request IDs.

High-level onboarding playlist (2-hour fast path):
1) Quickstart sprint (60-90 minutes)
   - Run language quickstart for your primary language (Node/Python/Go/Rust).
   - Validate streaming and non-streaming flows.
   - Confirm token accounting and a single embedding call.
2) Canonical API examples (20-30 minutes)
   - Execute a deterministic generation example and an embeddings example.
   - Capture golden output for local test harness.
3) Snippet authoring & docs preview (30-45 minutes)
   - Author a snippet using dx-snippet tooling, run local validation, open PR, and view staging preview.
4) Support handoff drill (15-30 minutes)
   - Create a compact repro, attach logs and expected output, and submit a mock handoff to the support queue.

Services and ownership (who to page):
- Docs-site and preview pipeline: eng-developer-experience/docs-team (service: docs-cms, runner: docs-build-runner).
- Snippet CI and validation: devx-ci team (service: snippet-validator).
- SDK CI and releases: sdk-engineering (service: sdk-ci, bot: sdk-release-bot).
- Support triage and escalation: customer-success/support (service: support-runbook).

Day-zero checklist for an authoring change:
- Obtain a sandbox API key and store in .env.local as REDWOOD_API_KEY.
- Run the language quickstart: `npm ci && npm run quickstart` or `python -m examples.quickstart`.
- Confirm the following calls succeed: 1) short generation, 2) streaming generation, 3) embedding.
- Create a docs PR that includes the snippet, a short description, and a golden-output file if applicable.

Snippet lifecycle (author -> validate -> preview -> promote):
1. Authoring
   - Use dx-snippet tooling: `dx-snippet init --lang python --template streaming` and replace env placeholders.
   - Include a clear expected-output header and test assertion for golden tests.
2. Local validation
   - Run `dx-snippet validate ./snippets/my-example` which runs syntax, lint, secret-scan, and golden diff checks.
3. CI gates
   - snippet-validator job checks: syntax, security-scan, golden-diff tolerance (< 3 tokens default), and runtime smoke against staging sandbox.
   - If a snippet fails due to nondeterminism, add a tolerances.json and mark the test flaky in comments for reviewer guidance.
4. Staging preview
   - docs-build-runner generates a preview URL for the PR. Execute the live snippet against staging and confirm behavior.
5. Promotion
   - After approvals and green CI, merge to main. Docs publish windows occur daily at 02:00 UTC. Use the hotfix path for critical fixes.

Key commands and examples:
- Local snippet validation: `dx-snippet validate --path snippets/quickstart-node`
- Create preview: `make docs-preview BRANCH=my-feature`
- Local full build: `make docs-local-build`
- Emergency publish: `scripts/publish-hotfix.sh --page docs/snippets/critical-fix`

SDK release & rollback guidance (practical):
- Before release: run full sdk-ci matrix and ensure snippet-validator is green for sample snippets.
- Canary: publish canary package to npm/registry and monitor metrics for 2 hours.
- Abort/rollback criteria: >= 5% error rate delta or critical production failures.
- Simple rollback example (npm): `npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk@X.Y.Z latest` to reassign the stable tag to the previous good version.

Support handoff template (required fields):
1) Brief summary (1-2 lines): what failed and who is affected.
2) Minimal repro: runnable snippet or curl that reproduces the error.
3) Environment details: sandbox|prod, region, model id, sdk version, runtime id.
4) Request IDs and logs: include client logs and server trace IDs.
5) Expected vs actual output: attach golden token excerpt or embedding checksum.
6) Impact and mitigation: number of users affected, temporary workaround, and urgency.

Canonical fixes for common patterns (quick reference):
- Stale API keys after rotation:
  Fix: confirm the new key landed in the environment, run `dx-snippet validate`, and add a one-off smoke test in sdk-ci to detect expired keys.
- Streaming reconnects interrupt mid-response:
  Fix: implement resumable stream pattern with a resume_id and exponential backoff. Sample pseudo-code provided below.
- Golden diffs caused by model bumps:
  Fix: pin model minor versions in examples, and use the golden-update workflow: create a golden update PR, label `golden-update`, and run full evals in the eval-harness.

Resumable stream pattern (pseudo-code):
```
let attempt = 0;
while (attempt < 5) {
  const stream = openStream({ resume_id });
  try {
    await stream.consume((chunk) => {
      process(chunk);
      // update resume_id from last ack
    });
    break;
  } catch (err) {
    await sleep(Math.pow(2, attempt) * 100);
    attempt += 1;
  }
}
```

Operational SLOs and alerts (set in dashboards):
- docs-build-runner: daily success >= 99%; page if failure rate > 2% in 1 hour.
- snippet-validator: pass rate >= 98%; alert on 3 consecutive flakes.
- preview render latency: p95 < 2s.

Runbook quick triage snippets:
- Staging preview 500: check logs `kubectl logs -l app=docs-cms -n staging --since=1h`, check job `kubectl describe job docs-build-runner`. If snippet-validator failed, revert the PR and notify the author with logs.
- SDK auth failures: validate key with `curl -v https://api.redwood.test/v1/auth/validate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY"` and verify rotation propagation through ops/kms/rotation-status.

Training ramp (first week):
- Day 0: run quickstart sprint, validate snippets locally.
- Day 1: author an API example and open a docs PR; pair-review with a maintainer.
- Day 2: join a 4-hour support shift to observe real triage and handoffs.
- Week 1: present a mini-retro and update canonical fixes and snippet guidance.

Appendix: useful links and artifacts:
- Snippets directory: `docs/snippets/` in docs repo.
- SDK starter templates: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-templates.
- Golden test runner: eval-harness/golden-runner (applied-ml-and-evals).
- Support runbook: /confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/support-runbook.

Change log:
- 2024-08-15: Initial draft and checklist.
- 2024-10-01: Added snippet-validator CI gate details.
- 2025-02-12: Updated SLOs and added resumable stream pattern.

Contacts and escalation:
- Docs-site owner: eng-developer-experience/docs-team (#docs-oncall).
- SDK releases: sdk-engineering (#sdk-release-oncall).
- Support triage: customer-success/support (#support-oncall).

Notes:
Keep examples minimal and reproducible. Prefer linking to deep playbooks for full-run procedures. Follow the four-step snippet lifecycle for every new example: author, validate, preview, promote.
